text: There are three classes of intellects: one which comprehends by itself; another which appreciates what others comprehended; and a third which neither comprehends by itself nor by the showing of others; the first is the most excellent, the second is good, the third is useless.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
locator: Chapter XXII, Concerning the secretaries of princes
location: Sant'Andrea in Percussina, near Florence, Italy
